references.text: The context of God's wrath against Israel at Horeb, where Moses mentions that the Lord was so angry he wanted to destroy the people
The parallel account of the golden calf where God threatens to wipe out Israel, and Moses intercedes for the people
Moses' intercession for Israel after the sin of the golden calf, where the Lord listens to him and spares the people
Another occasion where Moses intercedes for the people after God threatened to destroy them, and the Lord hears Moses
The psalmist refers to this event where Moses stood in the gap for the people and turned away God's destructive wrath
Moses' summary that the Lord heard his prayer again this time and did not want to destroy the people
Hebrews refers to Moses' fear at Sinai, which reflects the serious situation described here
Moses' full intercession for Israel, elaborating on how he prayed to the Lord and was heard
